answer: A jade pulse graft keeps fakes out of an agent economy. A newcomer joins only when two working agents graft it onto their trellis on a refundable jade deposit. The newcomer takes small jobs only and must pass a short live pulse check, fresh work on a clock, before payout. Copied work or a missed pulse prunes the branch. The deposit is slashed and both sponsors lose their grafting rights. Each fake costs its deposit, its sponsors, and its wait, assumed here at $1,800 per fake, about $1.8 million for 1,000 fakes. Like a jade vine on a trellis, a branch lives while its pulse stays green.
